CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: ultra

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Never drop not/never/no/only/except — flip meaning worse than any token saved. Numbers, units exact.

Never ADD word to sound caveman. Compression only — style never grow output. No inserted pronoun or copula to fake broken grammar: "when it not" cost one token more than "when not" and say same thing. Keep correct verb form when correct form cost same — "sees" one token, "see" one token, so mangle buy nothing and read worse. Same rule as abbreviations and arrows: if caveman phrasing not shorter than plain phrasing, use plain.

Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer — never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.

Preserve user's dominant language exactly — reply in the language user writes, never switch regardless of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. Compress the style, not the language. Every emitted line in that language — openings, pre-tool status lines, all — not just final reply. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

'Drop articles' = article languages only. Where small markers carry case/role (particles, postpositions), keep them — grammar, not filler; compress politeness/filler instead.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **ultra** | Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X → Y) — measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- ultra: "Inline obj prop, new ref, re-render. `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- ultra: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No per-request handshake."

Classical chars = wenyan modes only. Never swap a word to a classical char to shrink at non-wenyan levels.

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example shows FORMAT only — write warning in session language, not example's.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Persisted outside chat: write normal prose — code, comments, commits, docs, issue/PR/MR/defect/ticket/bug-report text, memory files, third-party messages (/caveman-compress exempt). "Open a defect" or "file a bug" mean the same as "open issue": body go to other humans, so body normal English. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

> **Why this file exists:** `viewer_template.html` is authored as minified one-line-per-block
> CSS/JS, so `git diff` reports a handful of 3,000-character line replacements and tells you
> nothing. This is the readable changelog for it.

---

## A. Committed since the pull

Two commits, both authored locally and already pushed.

| Commit | Title |
|---|---|
| `11f74b0` | Add scroll-driven bone landing experience |
| `b0a8dc2` | Use realistic femur for scroll landing |

```

autoimplants/viewer.py                   |  11 ++-

```

What landed:

- **Scroll-driven landing story.** A sticky 3D stage with the femur rendered behind three
  scroll-linked narrative beats, replacing the old static hero. New CSS surfaces:
  `.landing-story`, `.story-stage`, `.landing-canvas-shell`, `.story-beats`, `.story-beat`,
  `.story-heading`, `.story-copy`, `.story-kicker`, `.landing-fallback`, `.mesh-credit`.
- **Case intake split out** of the hero into its own section below the story:
  `.case-intake-section`, `.case-intake-copy`, `.intake-note`, `.upload-head`.
- **Landing chrome**: `.intake-nav-actions`, `.nav-start`, `.over-intake` (nav colour
  inversion on scroll), `.skip-link`, `.intake-assurance`, `.workflow-ledger`,
  `.workflow-item`, `.export-actions`, `.export-buttons`.
- **A real femur for the hero** — [autoimplants/viewer.py:36-49](autoimplants/viewer.py#L36-L49)
  now ships a separate `landing_mesh` payload (`LANDING_BONE_ASSET`,
  `LANDING_BONE_FACE_BUDGET = 10000`, `LANDING_BONE_COLOR = "#e7e0d4"`) so the landing object
  is decoupled from case anatomy.
- **Asset provenance** recorded in [autoimplants/assets/README.md](autoimplants/assets/README.md):
  *Human femur.stl* by Eric Bauer / Elon University anatomy lab, CC BY 4.0, decimated
  173,578 → 10,000 faces, with the optimized asset's SHA-256.
- 54 lines of viewer tests to cover it.

---

## B. Uncommitted UI work in the working tree

`git diff --stat` on the UI files:

```
autoimplants/viewer.py            |  2 +-
autoimplants/viewer_template.html | 26 ++++++------
tests/test_viewer.py              | 22 +++++++++++
```

CSS surfaces added on top of HEAD: `.story-diagram` (+ `--row`, `--stacked`), `.sd-node`,
`.sd-box`, `.sd-ico`, `.sd-op`, `.sd-join`, `.sd-down`, `.sd-cycle`, `.sd-logo`, `.sd-brand`,
`.story-glyph`, `.story-actions`, `.page-footer`, `.page-disclaimer`, `.footnote-ref`,
`.footnote-mark`. Removed: `.story-kicker`.

### B1 — Story diagrams (the `sd-*` system)

The narrative beats gained inline line-art diagrams instead of prose alone.

- **Beat 0, stacked** (`.story-diagram--stacked`): `[Femur mesh] + [Surgical plan]` → arrow →
  a bordered `.sd-box` holding `[Patient bone]` and `[Tailored plate]`.
- **Beat 1, row** (`.story-diagram--row`): `[Devin] ⟷ [Test]` joined by a two-arc `.sd-cycle`
  loop glyph.
- Shared vocabulary: `.sd-ico` (2.4px white stroke, the primary glyph), `.sd-op` (2px at .78
  opacity, secondary detail), `.sd-join` / `.sd-down` (connectors), `.sd-box` (2.4px white
  border, radius 16), `.sd-node` (76px column, uppercase 10px caption).
- Beat 1 also carries a `.story-actions` checklist: *Devin reads failure reports · Rewrites the
  design script · Rebuilds and re-validates the solid · Commits the reasoning change.*

### B2 — Devin brand mark

The `Devin` node's generic rotated-square glyph was replaced with the real Cognition logo
from [artifacts/cognition_logo.png](artifacts/cognition_logo.png), embedded as a
**base64 `data:` URI** so the template stays self-contained (0 external `src=` refs; the page
is served/opened standalone and must not depend on a repo-relative path).

- Source 750×750 RGBA → cropped to artwork (608×698) → resized to 77×88 → 6,158 B PNG →
  8,212 B base64.
- Sits on a `.sd-logo` white rounded tile (58px, 78px at the wide breakpoint). The tile is
  **required, not decoration**: the logo's darkest hex is `#2a6dce` against the story's
  `#5f8bb0` ground ≈ 1.5:1 contrast, so bare on the background its upper-left hexagons
  disappear. The tile also keeps the node the same footprint as its siblings so connectors
  and captions stay aligned.
- The sibling `Test` node reuses the tile with `.sd-brand` — stroke `url(#devin-ramp)`, a linear
  gradient in the Cognition ramp (`#2a6dce` → `#1796e2` → teal) — so the brand colour carries
  across the pair.

### B3 — Bone glyph: two lobes per end

`d="M17.5 17C13.4 18.1 …"` in the beat-0 diagram. The first attempt read as **three** bumps
per end: the segment between the two lobes had control points at y≈8.4 while the lobe crests
were at y≈9.6, so the "notch" arched *higher* than the lobes it separated, making a third,
tallest bump in the middle. Rebuilt so the inter-lobe segment dips to y≈14.1 against crests
at y≈10.8 — two lobes, one notch, mirrored top and bottom about y=28.

### B4 — Tailored plate glyph

- Plate `rect` from `6×22 rx 3.5` to a thinner, longer `5×38 rx 2.5`, so it reads as a plate
  rather than a block and is visibly thinner than the bone shaft.
- The three tick marks that sat *outside* the old plate became three screw holes on the plate
  centreline. They needed their own thin class — a 2px stroke on a 1.3-radius circle renders
  as a solid blob at 44px.
- ⚠️ The requested soft-edge square was first built as `.sd-frame` (48×48 `rx 12`, 1.5px white
  stroke at .34 opacity over a `rgba(255,255,255,.05)` fill, in a 56-unit viewBox). It has since
  been **superseded** by wrapping the two nodes in the existing `.sd-box` border instead;
  `.sd-frame` and `.sd-hole` are gone from the file. The rebuilt bone path survived the swap.

### B5 — Implant reads as metal, not glass

The plate in the workbench viewer looked like transparent glass. Alpha was never the cause —
`toMesh` has always set `alpha: 1`. The cause was tone: the shared bone/implant curve peaked
at a 1.5 multiplier, which pushed the light steel-blue base to a near-white `rgb(215,244,255)`
across a wide band of front-facing triangles.

Two passes on this, and ⚠️ **the second overwrote the first**:

| | Colour | Shading |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | `#8fa3b0` | shared curve, `.42 + .72·l + .36·l⁸` |
| Pass 1 (this session) | `#8b9095` neutral gray | `.54 + .46·l + .26·l¹⁴` — tighter specular, peak 1.26 |
| **Current tree** | `#c8ccd2` light silver | `metalTone(nx,ny,nz,l)` — reflection-vector environment ramp + horizon band + Fresnel edge term |

`metalTone` is the more physical answer and is what the file now calls from the tone
expression in `createMeshRenderer.draw`; the pass-1 constants are gone.
[autoimplants/viewer.py:48](autoimplants/viewer.py#L48) carries the matching colour.

### B6 — Footer, footnote, copy

- New `.page-footer` / `.page-disclaimer` with a `.footnote-ref` superscript from the intake
  assurance line: *"13 geometry checks · 8 stress checks¹"* → research-use disclaimer.
- `.story-kicker` ("Autonomous implant engineering") removed.
- Beat headings rewritten (as committed at HEAD → current tree): *"Start with the anatomy."* → *"Start with
  **your** patient's anatomy."*; *"The agent changes the shape."* → *"Deploy Cognition Devin
  to iteratively improve the plate's shape & fit."*; *"Only validated solids reach review."* →
  *"Agentic loop."* + the sub *"Human oversight reduced to final clinical sign-off."*

### B7 — Dialog cancel could not cancel

`tests/test_viewer.py` gained `test_cancel_buttons_skip_form_validation`: a `<button>` inside a
`<form>` defaults to `type=submit`, so Cancel ran HTML5 validation on the required reviewer
name and acknowledgement checkbox, the submit was blocked, the `onsubmit` router never saw the
submitter, and there was no way out of the approve/revision dialogs without filling in the
decision you were trying to abort. The test pins `value="cancel" formnovalidate` on both
dialogs while keeping the fields required for the real decision paths.

Not UI, but uncommitted alongside it — worth separating before staging:

- **[autoimplants/dicom_to_mesh.py](autoimplants/dicom_to_mesh.py) (+63)** — `_validate_affine()`
